issues.text: Three expectations of my own oracle were wrong before the first run on the real code; each was corrected from the words of the requirement and the code was right every time: (1) in quotes after a scheme or Bearer, a quote followed by WHITE SPACE is the closing quote of a string and there is no value at all (F2, F8 text), so the row 'Authorization: Basic "<white space>your9"' is stored, not refused (sweeps Ybsq, Ybbq: the slot stored when it is white space, the quote or '$'); (2) 'xxx(' is a call (class V2: an identifier and then '('), '***(' is not - '*' is no identifier character; (3) as the FIRST character of a value a quote opens a string whose content is a literal (B1-B4 do not apply in quotes), so 'token: "{[(|>{[(' is refused. Two rows with quotes of two kinds after the colon of Authorization ("' and '") are refused, not stored: the first quote opens a string that is not closed on its line and the whole rest of the line is one non-empty quotation (the definition of a value in quotes); they are C63#3 and #4 without a stored partner.

Time: the bytes file alone is now 135.2 s (105.5 s at 08i), the seven files 135.6 s; the growth is the new rows (RB-11 about 15 s per input, RB-20 about 9 s per input). The bytes file is now the longest file of npm test, so the whole suite takes about the time of the bytes file. Criterion 7 (budget 120 s) belongs to the timing file, which is untouched. If TEST-RUNNER or the owner wants it shorter, the store pass of RB-20 (every third row) and RB-11 (every refused row, three inputs) can take a stride for the old sweeps; I did not weaken either.

F6 of 08j (the guard for a value that is not a string, mask.js line 1032): not a rule of the requirement and not in my order; I did not add an assertion for a behaviour the requirement does not state. The two mechanical mutants (indices 1990, 1991) are named SILENT in the sweep numbers above; the harness probe 'non-string' that counted them killed is taken out of my screen, so the screen now equals the shipped tests.

Reading taken from the letter of the requirement and worth one sentence at the next requirement edit (like F9 of 08j): the marker '-----BEGIN' and the prefixes sk-, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, eyJ are written in one case; the code and the tables read them case-sensitively (as the old rules M1 and M4-M6 did), so '-----begin PRIVATE KEY-----', 'SK-...', 'GHP_...', 'akia...', 'EYJ.a.b' are stored (sweeps CXpem, CXsk, CXgh, CXpat, CXak, CXjwt). The text does not say 'in any case' for them, and it does for Bearer, the names, the schemes and the 26 words.

AP-110 for the list, as proposed at 08j (I3) and now carried out: for every rule written as 'starts with', 'ends with', 'the whole value', 'only of', 'a run of', 'an optional one', 'any case' add a mutation class to the generator (contains, first k, exactly one / at most two, any number, case-sensitive / case-insensitive) next to the generic ones; the five classes are in gen2.mjs (about 150 lines) and find in seconds the survivors that a validator found by hand at 08h and 08j (33 of the 136 new mutants were alive on the tables of 08i, among them all seven named ones; 7 are alive now and all are equivalent).
